post.title: One Word Makes People Say Yes #shorts
post.description: Leo cuts the copier line with a reason that isn't a reason. In 1978 Harvard psychologists Ellen Langer, Arthur Blank and Benzion Chanowitz asked people at a copy machine to let someone go first with 5 pages. No reason: 60% agreed. "Because I'm in a rush": 94%. "Because I have to make copies" — no real reason at all: 93%. For a bigger favour (20 pages) the empty "because" stopped working: people only listen closely when it matters. #psychology #shorts #persuasion #influence
